subject: PayFlow: spike in gen latency during peak — runway, product asks, and customer comms
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PayFlow — sudden p95/p99 jump in us-west-2 during peak

Team,

We're seeing a sustained p95 and p99 latency increase for PayFlow's gen-api traffic in us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PST. Key symptoms:
- p50 up ~40% (normal ~120ms → 170ms)
- p95 up ~210% (normal ~350ms → ~1.1s)
- Throughput for their account down ~30% concurrent QPS (requests timing out/backpressure)

Attached is an error snapshot from our edge tracing and a short request sample. Their traffic is heavy on long-context streaming requests and uses a high-token window for few-shot prompts. This is impacting a live checkout flow.

Immediate asks:
1) Can SRE confirm any hotspot in kernel scheduling / KV cache miss spikes? (Ben)
2) Product: can we expose a routing override to send PayFlow to the fallback quantized model (lower perf risk) for the next 2–4 hours? (Stephanie)
3) Ops: please start a 30-minute bridge so we can triage and lock a mitigation path, then craft wording for PayFlow. I'll draft a short customer note once we have the chosen mitigation.

Attachments: error_snapshot_20280211.json

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayFlow — sudden p95/p99 jump in us-west-2 during peak

On Sat, Feb 11, 2028 at 09:12, Marissa Cole wrote:
> We're seeing a sustained p95 and p99 latency increase for PayFlow's gen-api traffic in us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PST.

Thanks — starting a bridge now (zoom link in calendar). Priorities for the next 90 minutes:
- Ben: surface top-5 traces and confirm if this is kernel-scheduling/Kv-cache or model-side latency. Share any quick grafana links so we can include in customer note.
- Soojin: check routing table and whether an immediate per-account override to route PayFlow to the v1.2-q fallback is trivial. If yes, please test on a single request and report back.
- Stephanie/Marissa: prep a 1–2 sentence customer-facing status that says we have identified increased tokenization/cache churn and are applying mitigation; give an ETA.

Product ask (short runway): if the per-account override is not in the console, can we ship an emergency flag (api/console) that existing SRE can flip for this account only? This should:
- route to quantized fallback v1.2-q (compatible API)
- disable streaming for long-token sessions for the account to avoid partial-response stalls

If the above is >60 minutes, we'll fallback to an infra-side mitigation (cache warming + temporary autoscale). Please call out any quality degradation expected from v1.2-q in your reply.

I'll own customer comms once we decide.

-Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Platform & Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayFlow — sudden p95/p99 jump in us-west-2 during peak

Quick diagnostic notes from the bridge:
- KV cache miss rate for PayFlow shard usw2-a jumped from 8% → 46% coincident with the spike. Eviction rate increased due to higher token-window variance and a recent tokenizer shipping change (recent release: token-split heuristics v0.9.3).
- Kernel queuing metrics show increased tail wait on multi-tenant scheduler on nodes handling large-context sessions. We haven't observed OOMs; it's queuing/backpressure.

Short-term mitigations (immediate):
1) Route PayFlow traffic to fallback model v1.2-q (quantized) — temporary quality dip expected for subtle completions (expected BLEU/Lex change minimal for structured prompts; free-text completions may show slightly more conservative responses). Estimated push time: ~10–15 minutes for per-account routing flip.
2) Disable streaming for long-token sessions for PayFlow — prevents partial-stream stalls and reduces in-flight kernel pressure. Toggleable at the routing proxy layer; push in ~5 minutes.
3) Apply targeted cache-warm for PayFlow's common prefixes (warming script attached). This will reduce misses over ~20–40 minutes.
4) Increase autoscale target on the dedicated pool for us-west-2 by +2 nodes (hot standby) — request submitted to infra and will take ~12 minutes to fully initialize.

If product can't deliver per-account override within 60 minutes, we'll do 1–3 infra-side. After mitigations, we'll monitor p95/p99 and consider a short canary of the regular model for a subset of requests.

Attachments: mitigation_checklist_v1.pdf (checklist + warming script)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Staff SRE | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayFlow — sudden p95/p99 jump in us-west-2 during peak

Thanks for the fast triage. A couple product/roadmap notes and questions:
- Quality trade-off: we need concrete numbers to commit to PayFlow. Ben, can you capture a short eval (50 sample requests from their recent traffic window) showing delta in token repeat rate, hallucination flags, and average token-latency between prod model and v1.2-q? If the quality regression is tolerable for their checkout UX, we'll default to the per-account shortcut for future similar incidents.
- Short runway product work: we should scope a lightweight per-account routing override toggle in the console (owner or SE can flip). ETA for an emergency UI + API flag: 2–3 sprints (but we should try to get a CLI/api-only flip in <48 hours).
- Longer term: can we add a routing policy that automatically routes accounts to a fallback model when per-account p95 > threshold for 5 consecutive minutes? This will be a roadmap ask — include cost guardrails.

Customer comms: approve the brief note with the mitigation path (route to v1.2-q, disable streaming, cache warm, ETA 4 hours). We should offer a credit for partial outage: suggested 10% for impacted day's usage and a postmortem within 72 hours.

I will follow up with PM PRD notes after the immediate bridge.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Product Manager, Serving | Redwood Inference
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex@payflow.com>, Priya Desai <procurement@payflow.com>, PayFlow Ops <ops@payflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Feb 2028 13:47:00 -0800
Subject: Update: mitigation in place for latency spike (PayFlow) — next steps and credits

Alex/Priya —

Thank you for your patience this morning on the PayFlow impact. Quick status update and what we did:
- What happened: an increase in KV cache miss and kernel queuing on the us-west-2 serving pool caused elevated p95/p99 latency for long-context streaming requests, which impacted your checkout flow. We traced this to a tokenizer heuristics change that increased token-window variance for some prompts.
- Immediate mitigation applied (completed at 13:20 PST):
  • We routed PayFlow traffic to our fallback quantized model (v1.2-q) to reduce kernel pressure.
  • Streaming for long-token sessions has been temporarily disabled for your account to avoid partial response stalls.
  • Targeted cache-warming for common prefixes initiated.
  • We added +2 nodes to the us-west-2 dedicated pool as hot-standby.

Impact & ETA: these actions reduced p95 by ~60% from peak; throughput is recovering. We expect full stabilization within ~4 hours as cache warms.

Compensation: we will apply a 10% credit to today’s impacted usage for PayFlow as a gesture of goodwill and will provide a full incident postmortem within 72 hours.

Next steps (internal owners):
- Ben: monitor p95/p99 and confirm when traffic can be gradually routed back.
- Stephanie/Product: prepare a short PRD for the per-account routing override + automated fallback policy.
- Marissa/CS: schedule a 30-minute customer follow-up call tomorrow to walk through remediation and next steps.
- Nikhil: lead the postmortem and coordinate the credits.

If you'd like an immediate screenshare to walk through the mitigation, I'm available at 14:30 PST. Again, apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the full write-up.

Best,

Nikhil Sharma
